title: Rent parties and Harlem's money and safety in the Depression
summary: Holmes recalls Harlem as full of night life and cash during the Depression, safe at any hour with doors left unlocked.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Now, what about things like Harlem rent parties? Did you get involved in any of those?
What is a Harlem rent party?
Well, it's supposed to be where someone can't afford to pay his rent, and then has a party, and the piano player... I guess it was mostly the piano players...
A Harlem rent party is just another house

rent party. That's all it is. It's a house rent party. Somebody... Well, at that time, I mean, things were tough. And the funny thing, there was more night life going on in Harlem then than there is now, and there was more money in circulation in Harlem... Well, I wouldn't put it like that, because there's an awful lot of money in circulation now. But I mean, they were talking about conditions being hard and bad, but there was a lot of money in circulation in Harlem. And this was back in the Depression days. A lot of money was in circulation. And people were jumping out of windows downtown in the financial section; they were getting wiped out by the stock market and jumping out of windows. It wasn't safe to walk the streets downtown. And up here in Harlem, they were ballin' morning, noon and night! Wasn't nothin' else could happen. Good times was the thing of the day.

And you could walk anywhere you wanted at any hour of the night. Nobody would bother you. People would be out in the street. There would be just as many out on the street at three or four or five o'clock in the morning as there would be in the afternoon. You'd always find people in the street. Always! Nobody was rippin' off anybody. Nobody was getting ripped off. People would go out and leave their doors unlocked, and go away, and go out for dancing or any
place else they wanted to go, and come back, and the place would still be there, with doors unlocked and everything. Nobody would bother you. But that's a long time ago. Not like it is now.
